title: Clinical investigation of sex-dependent effects on migraine - a prospective questionnaire-based study
summary: Migraine is a highly prevalent primary headache disorder which affects 10-15% of the general population. The prevalence of migraine is well known to be highly dysproportinal with a female to male ratio of 3-4:1. This fact points to an important role of sex and sex hormones for migraine. This is further supported by the fact that female migraine attacks are frequently triggered by menstruation. So far, little is known about sex-dependent effects on the clinical presentation of migraine. However, some clinical data indicate that migraine symptoms of males are less prominent thant those of females. At worst, this may more frequently result in a delayed or even false diagnosis in male migraineurs as compared to female migraineurs. We will perform a  a questionnaire-based study in order to further characterize putative sex effects on migraine.

interventions.name:
This is a questionnaire-based study. The questionnaire is filled-in by headache patients with the following diagnoses:
1) migraine without aura, 
2) migraine with aura, 
3) probable migraine without aura, 
4) probable migraine with aura,

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1) Patients fulfilling the diagnostic criteria for either definite of probable episodic or chronic migraine with or without aura according to the International Classification of Headache Disorders (ICHD) 3rd edition,
2) history of headache > 1 year
3) good German language skills
Exclusion criteria:
Migraine patients with concomitant other primary headache disorders, who are not able to distinguish between their headache syndromes
